files_actually_read: nodes/_otr_ledger_cleanup.py (grep for PROTECTED_FACT_COMPONENT_FLAG only, body not read)
verdict: The driver's anchor is unusually well-grounded: every symbol-cited claim I checked held up, and I additionally live-spot-checked the actual shipped ledger on disk (not just the code path), which corroborates the defect end to end -- including that `announcer_intro_rewrite.status == "announcer_intro_rewritten"` and that the shipped row already carries `unclean_spoken_text` (`UNCLEAN_COMPOSE_FLAG`) from `run_ledger_clean`. The controlling mechanics risk the anchor did not surface is sequencing plus protection: the no-locator/subtitle branch needs `meta["episode_title"]`, which is deliberately not bound until J.5 (`OTR_LedgerScriptWriter.py` ~6434), strictly AFTER both announcer-intro compose call sites (~5875 in-loop, ~6107 rewrite); and any text spliced into that row before `run_ledger_clean` runs (~6880) is exposed to being judged/rewritten unless stamped `PROTECTED_FACT_COMPONENT_FLAG` -- proven live, since that exact pass already touched this exact row in the defective episode.
where_the_shape_breaks: If the deterministic no-locator/subtitle clause is computed inside compose_announcer_intro (nodes/_otr_line_composer.py) at either call site (OTR_LedgerScriptWriter.py line ~5875 in-loop or ~6107 rewrite), the episode's own final title is not yet bound -- meta["episode_title"]/final_title is set at J.5 (OTR_LedgerScriptWriter.py ~6434), which runs strictly after both compose sites -- so the subtitle half renders empty or None.

If a builder splices the naming clause into the announcer row's text via _otr_ledger.patch_line_text (the same primitive _apply_intro_rewrite_result already uses at OTR_LedgerScriptWriter.py ~2250) at any point before run_ledger_clean (OTR_LedgerScriptWriter.py ~6880) without stamping PROTECTED_FACT_COMPONENT_FLAG (_otr_ledger_clean.py) on that row's compose_flags, the clause is exposed to run_ledger_clean's judge-and-repair pass -- live-proven: line b001 of the shipped defective ledger already carries 'unclean_spoken_text' (UNCLEAN_COMPOSE_FLAG, _otr_ledger_clean.py line 138) from that exact pass.

If the new splice derives its work-title/gate decision by calling _otr_source_identity.identity_from_meta(meta).work_title fresh, or reads meta['source_identity']['work_title'], instead of consuming the already-gated `_work_title` local computed once in OTR_LedgerScriptWriter.run (~4080-4091), it reopens the media_archive collision: identity_from_meta returns work_title = the publisher/source_label (e.g. 'Now See Hear!') for media_archive with no gate of its own -- ADAPTATION_SOURCE_KINDS is applied at exactly one choke point today (OTR_LedgerScriptWriter.py line 4089).

If public_domain's unit_label is rendered as a locator unconditionally, single-story units where unit_label == title verbatim stutter -- confirmed live in config/source_banks/public_domain_story/manifest.sample.json: canterville_ghost's source['title'] == 'The Canterville Ghost' and its sole unit's label == 'The Canterville Ghost', so an unde-duped render would say 'The Canterville Ghost, "The Canterville Ghost"'.

_otr_ledger_cleanup.run_ledger_cleanup (called immediately after run_ledger_clean, OTR_LedgerScriptWriter.py ~6888) has zero PROTECTED_FACT_COMPONENT_FLAG references (grepped, no hits) and its own module docstring says it can blank an unsayable row out of the voiced set -- a spliced clause protected only against run_ledger_clean could still be at risk here; this needs the driver/panel to check its body, which I did not fully read.
recommendations: Implement the naming clause as ONE new deterministic step inserted strictly after J.5's final_title binds (OTR_LedgerScriptWriter.py ~6434) and strictly before run_ledger_clean (~6880) -- not as a change inside compose_announcer_intro's prompt context -- so the locator and no-locator/subtitle branches share one mechanism and the subtitle race is structurally impossible rather than merely avoided.

Strip WORK entirely out of compose_announcer_intro's context tuple (delete the ("WORK", _work_line(...)) entry, nodes/_otr_line_composer.py ~1446) and reword _ANNOUNCER_INTRO_SYSTEM_SAFE (~1170) to tell the model the work is named separately -- removing the model's OPPORTUNITY to author a title, not just re-instructing it not to, consistent with the anchor's own 'supplying the fact is necessary and not sufficient' finding.

Stamp PROTECTED_FACT_COMPONENT_FLAG on the announcer-intro row's compose_flags in the same new step that splices the clause in, mirroring compose_news_coda's existing pattern for this exact hazard class (PBUG-20260815-01).

Feed the new step from the already-gated `_work_title` local (OTR_LedgerScriptWriter.py ~4087-4091), never from a fresh identity_from_meta(meta).work_title read, to keep the media_archive gate at its single existing choke point.
Dedupe public_domain's unit_label locator against title (normalized) before rendering it; when equal, fall through to the no-locator/subtitle shape instead.

Read _otr_ledger_cleanup.run_ledger_cleanup's body before implementation to confirm it either already respects a protection flag under a different name or genuinely needs the same PROTECTED_FACT_COMPONENT_FLAG check added.
must_fix: The sequencing gap: the no-locator/subtitle branch needs meta['episode_title'], which is not bound until J.5, but both existing announcer-intro compose call sites run before J.5 -- the fix must be a post-J.5 splice, not an in-prompt or in-compose change, or the subtitle branch ships broken.
The PROTECTED_FACT_COMPONENT_FLAG gap: without it, run_ledger_clean (proven live to already touch this exact row) remains free to rewrite/strip a spliced deterministic clause.
The gating source: the splice must consume the already-gated `_work_title`, never a fresh identity_from_meta(meta).work_title call, or the media_archive collision (item F's r3 catch) reopens.
